### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2678600d57f70f6913384f03f65c12e480781486`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2678600d57f70f6913384f03f65c12e480781486` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6ae9693ba6f344adc023f681fa768b2e7252907d` — the merge of head `9d2ea03212cd21decb9f39bb24c1d1284986594f` into base `2678600d57f70f6913384f03f65c12e480781486`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6ae9693ba6f344adc023f681fa768b2e7252907d && git checkout 6ae9693ba6f344adc023f681fa768b2e7252907d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2678600d57f70f6913384f03f65c12e480781486 9d2ea03212cd21decb9f39bb24c1d1284986594f && git checkout -B drift-repro 2678600d57f70f6913384f03f65c12e480781486 && git merge --no-ff 9d2ea03212cd21decb9f39bb24c1d1284986594f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2678600d57f70f6913384f03f65c12e480781486
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2678600d57f70f6913384f03f65c12e480781486` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9d2ea03212cd21decb9f39bb24c1d1284986594f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts, packages/cli/test/build-override-declarations.test.ts, packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts + packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts (step 3a-iii, ≈:664–690, unchanged), packages/cli/src/utils/override-declarations.ts (`findOverrideDeclarationRefusals`, unchanged), packages/cli/src/utils/format.ts (`emitJson`), packages/cli/vitest-tiers.ts (`isIntegration`), scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs; the changeset `.changeset/28643-build-override-write-gate.md` is a prose face (the seat's ACCEPT reads it sentence by sentence) and is read here only for ②
Inputs: card #28643 (triage `6557795179` answer A, claim `6557871622`, os-dev-report `6558473696`), the order `pm-orders/server/order-28643.md`, PR #28681 body, diff `0b6a52e8..9d2ea032` (merge-base with `origin/main`, 4 files, +230/−15, two commits: `3ed0c554` the fix, `9d2ea032` the changeset's ADR-0087 line), the head's check-runs (read 2026-11-01T13:22Z: 45 latest-per-name runs, 22 success + 13 skipped + 10 in progress — `Lint ·` ×6, `Test Core` 1–8, `Type Check ·` ×3, `Live E2E UI` — none failed; `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Test UI` green), the source context: card #28410, PR #28554 and its record `6556791212` (note 1).
Face: narrowing — `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset, declared the same on both; `record-recognisers --paths` on the four paths decides no schema or governed face and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②:` line, which carries the `(narrowing)` arm, so the tier is `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` and the Scope floor is every diff path outside the prose faces (all three code paths above).

### ① Derived judgments

1. One judge, no second spelling. `compile.ts` step 3b-iii calls `findOverrideDeclarationRefusals(result.data as Record<string, unknown>)`, the identical call `validate.ts` makes at 3a-iii (:671) on the identical input (`result.data`, the parsed stack after the key lints, the lowering and the parse). The walk (`utils/override-declarations.ts`) and the verdict (`judgeOverrideWrite`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`) are reused unchanged; the rows (`path`, `code: 'NOT_OVERRIDABLE'`, `rule`, `packageId`, `message`) reach the `--json` face as `errors` untouched and the text face as `PATH [CODE] MESSAGE` from the same fields. Nothing of the judge or its sentences is re-spelled. Right, and it is answer A as ruled.
2. Same exit code, no artifact. On any row: `--json` emits this command's failure envelope (`{ success: false, errors, warnings: warningsSoFar(), conversions }`, the exact shape step 3a's #20393 view-container refusal uses at :479) and `this.exit(1)`; text prints the heading and bullets and `this.exit(1)`. `os validate` exits 1 on the same rows (its envelope is `valid: false`, the command's own shape — the test compares `errors`, the shared part, not the envelope key). Every artifact write in `compile.ts` sits later: the access-matrix snapshot (:969, step 3d) and `fs.writeFileSync(artifactPath, …)` (:1257, step 4). The `catch`/re-throw of oclif's exit signal is the established pattern of the steps above it (`isExitSignal`, `format.ts`). Right.
3. Placement. The ruling said "beside `checkDependencyRanges`" and that is where it sits (3b-iii, immediately ahead of 3b-quater). `os validate` runs the gate earlier (3a-iii, before its 3b capability preflight and 3e dependency ranges); the order changes only which refusal a stack with several defects hears first, never the accept set, since both commands refuse before any write. Right; the PR's acceptance note says the same.
4. The text heading. `The publish door would refuse N item(s) under the override write gate (ADR-0146 D2)` is spelled once in `compile.ts` (:797) and once in `validate.ts` (:685). It is presentation text, not the judge and not a refusal message: the sentence per item is the judge's own `message`, the code and path are the walker's. The same heading-in-two-places shape is the #20393 precedent on `main` (`The server would refuse this stack at boot`, `validate.ts`:442 and `compile.ts`:484), and folding it into an export (`picklistRefusalHeading` shape, `utils/picklist-references.ts`:452) edits `validate.ts`, outside the claim's file surface. The new test pins the build's block (heading + bullets) EQUAL to `os validate`'s, so the two spellings cannot drift silently. Acceptable; not a second spelling of the judge in the sense the ruling forbids. Noted as a fold for the next card that opens `validate.ts` (note 1 below).
5. The parity ledger. `findOverrideDeclarationRefusals` leaves `VALIDATE_ONLY_GATES` (now `{}`, its documented steady state) and joins `SHARED_NON_REGISTRY_GATES`. The file is a closed source-level roster: it extracts every bare-identifier call site of `compile.ts` and `validate.ts` and asserts a SHARED row is called by both, a VALIDATE_ONLY row by `validate.ts` alone (pruned both ways), and every name sits in exactly one ledger. On this head the gate is called by both commands, so leaving the row in `VALIDATE_ONLY_GATES` would have reddened the pin; moving it is the only correct spelling, and it is the #20393 move repeated (`findViewContainerNameRefusals`). Nothing outside this test reads either list: `grep` over the tree finds `VALIDATE_ONLY_GATES` / `SHARED_NON_REGISTRY_GATES` in `packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` only (the CHANGELOG mentions are prose); no census, gate or workflow consumes them. The header docblock now names both rows the ledger has held. Right.
6. Clean build unchanged. The new step reads the parsed stack, writes nothing, prints nothing and sets nothing when the row list is empty (no step line on either face, as on `os validate`); every write and every success payload is downstream of it. A clean stack's artifact is therefore byte-identical to base by construction; the dev's measured sha256 equality (`638c0fb8…b0b3a6`, pair control) and the CONTROL case agree. `validate.ts` is not in the diff, so `os validate` output is unchanged. Right.
7. The accept-to-refuse move is exactly the declared one. Newly refused at `os build` = the set `findOverrideDeclarationRefusals` returns non-empty for = the set `os validate` already refused under this gate = (by #28554's ①7/①8, record `6556791212`) what the publish doors and the managed install refuse with the same judge. Nothing else is refused: no new rule, no changed row, no door touched, no repo/CI gate added. The narrowing is real (an artifact `os build` emitted before is now refused) and delivers the spec's own refusal earlier; what any door accepts is unchanged. Declared on both carriers as `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Right.
8. Published surface. `@objectstack/cli` exports no type or value here; `override-declarations.ts` is not re-exported; `packages/spec/**` untouched; no `docs/adr/**`, no `skills/**` (`Skills-docs: none` on the PR body with its reason — `skills/objectstack-platform/references/operations.md` already says both commands run the same gates, which this diff makes true for one more). No `Clause-②: yes` arm is owed. Right.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/28643-build-override-write-gate.md`: `@objectstack/cli: patch`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Consistent with the three readers:

- `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` (the one reader) reads `no (narrowing)` as a declared `no` with the `narrowing` arm, and `none` as a declared kind of the closed set `added | narrowed | semantic | none`. Both lines are in the fixed spelling at line start on the PR body and the changeset alike.
- `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (ruling A on #25105): the level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` line alone — `none` ⇒ every introduced entry `patch`; its own self-test pins exactly this pair (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` + `Metadata-protocol: none` ⇒ `none-clean`, "a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING carriers"). The two cross-checks (`added` under `no`, `narrowed` beside no arm) do not fire. `none` is truthful: no key an author writes is added, removed or re-meant; the protocol a `defineStack` author writes against is unchanged, and the refusal moved earlier is the publish door's, already on `main`.
- `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`: the `(narrowing)` arm is a breaking signal (#16421), so a disposition is owed; `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is refused only when the body carries a migration prescription, and this body carries none (the remedy is the judge's own sentence — rename, or declare from `<base>.custom` — stated as prose, no FROM → TO section). The dev measured the gate red before `9d2ea032` and green after; `Check Changeset` is `completed/success` on this head.

So `patch` is the right level, `none` is accepted on a `(narrowing)` arm, and the disposition holds. The PR body's `Clause-②`, `Metadata-protocol` and `Skills-docs` lines read the same contract as the changeset. Note: the changeset carries no `**BREAKING**` banner; the ADR-0087 gate reads the arm itself as the signal, so no gate is owed one here, and #28554's banner belonged to its `yes (narrowing)` with exports widened. Not a must-fix.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on `9d2ea032` at 2026-11-01T13:22Z: 22 success, 13 skipped, 10 still in progress (the lint, Test Core, type-check and Live E2E families), none failed. This record judges the contract; the landing pre-check ② (全绿) is the seat's to re-read on this head before it queues. The suites that would catch the one behavioural change (`Test Core`) were still running at write time; the dev's reported run of the cli unit project (364 files / 5167 tests, exit 0 at `3ed0c554`, head adds a changeset line only) is the dev's claim, not read here.
- `open_questions: []`. One out-of-scope finding (the heading spelled twice): answered at ①4 — acceptable, not a must-fix; note 1.
- Test budget (order hypothesis "prefer in-process"): the new test runs `Compile.run` / `Validate.run` in-process (`Command.run(argv, { root })`, the `explain-rule-id.test.ts` spelling), no child process, no `runServe`, no `new ObjectQL(` — `vitest-tiers.ts`'s predicate places it in the `unit` project, and its name carries no `.e2e`/`.live`, so it is queue-tier. Three `mkdtemp` fixtures, four cases, 60 s ceilings; the first case pays the command-graph import (dev: 4.3 s). The stdout capture is sound: `disableConsoleIntercept: true` sends `console.log` to `process.stdout.write`, and the spy honours `emitJson`'s write callback so the drained-write path resolves. Sensible.
- Overlap: open PRs at 2026-11-01T13:22Z touching `packages/cli/`: only #28651 (`packages/cli/test/setup-integrations-order.pin.test.ts`); none touches `compile.ts`, `override-declarations.ts` or the parity test (#28679, #28674, #28671, #28670, #28669, #28668, #28667, #28651, #28499 read by file list; the rest are mailboxes and the release PR).
- Not a repo gate: the diff adds no workflow, script or lint; it is a product refusal inside one CLI command, as ruled.
- Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; draft; no auto-merge. No `docs/adr/**`, no `skills/**`, no `packages/spec/**`.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing face, judged against the published spec on `main`: ADR-0146 D2 says only the base's paired `<base>.custom` declares an override and a dependent's same-named item is refused; #28554 made that real at the save door, the promotion, `os validate` and the managed install, and recorded `os build` as the one authoring door that still emitted what every landing door refused. This diff makes the spec's own refusal real at the last producer door, with the same judge, the same walk, the same rows and the same exit code, and takes no declared capability away: a `.custom` declaring its base's item still builds (CONTROL), and a stack any door accepts builds byte-identically.

Tried to break it on this head:

- A different input to the judge. Both commands hand the judge `result.data`, the parsed stack; `compile.ts` runs `lowerCallables`, the key lints and `authoringRuleUnionStack` exactly as `validate.ts` does (the parity roster holds those as SHARED rows), so the walk sees the same packages, items and dependencies. The `undeclared` fixture (a `packages[]` stack) proves the per-package walk is reached from the build.
- Refusal after a write. No write precedes 3b-iii; the access-matrix snapshot and the artifact itself are steps 3d and 4.
- A `--json` double document. `emitJson` is awaited (buffer drained), then `this.exit(1)` throws oclif's exit signal, which the outer catch re-throws (the pattern of 3a, 3b-quater and every refusing step); the test parses stdout as one document and would catch a second.
- A second judge. `grep` of the diff: no `judgeOverrideWrite` call, no `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` literal, no rule name spelled in `compile.ts`; the test pins equality with `os validate`'s rows rather than a copy of the words, so a drift in the judge moves both commands together.
- The ledger lying. `VALIDATE_ONLY_GATES` is pruned both ways by the parity pin; an empty ledger with the gate in SHARED is the only shape the pin accepts on this head.

Findings: no must-fix.

1. Note for the next card that opens `validate.ts` (no fix here): fold the override-gate heading into one export beside the walk (`utils/override-declarations.ts`, the `picklistRefusalHeading` shape) and read it from both commands — and the #20393 boot-refusal heading with it. The test's block-equality pin keeps the two honest until then.
